title: Starting a small business
examples: How do I find a good business idea that people will actually buy?
What is the difference between costs and profit when I sell something?
If my costs are low, does that automatically mean I will make a lot of profit?

explain.say: Today we are learning about starting a small business.

items: Ideas need to solve a problem.
Customers decide if people want it.
Profit is what you earn after costs.

explain.say: First you need a good business idea. This is what you will sell.
For example, if you see people struggling to carry heavy groceries, your idea could be a delivery service.
Next you must find your customers. These are the people who will buy your idea.

items: Test Idea: Will they pay for it?
Refine: Make it better for them

explain.say: For instance, if your idea is custom dog treats, your customers are dog owners in your local area.
Finally, you must track your costs and profit. Profit is what is left over.

faq.q: What is the difference between costs and profit?
faq.a: Costs are all the money you spend to make or sell your product. Profit is the money you have left after you subtract all your costs from the money you earned.
asks: Is revenue the same as profit?

faq.q: Do I need to know my customers before I start?
faq.a: Yes, knowing your customers helps you make something they actually want to buy. You should ask them what they need.
asks: How do I find out what people want?
Is market research important for a small business?

faq.a: Costs include things like materials, electricity, and your own time spent making the product. Everything you spend money on is a cost.
asks: Do I count my time as a cost?
Are ingredients part of the cost?

faq.q: How do I make sure my idea is good enough?
faq.a: You can test your idea by making a small version and seeing if people are willing to buy it. This is called a pilot test.
asks: Should I sell it to friends first?
What is a minimum viable product?
How do I get feedback on my idea?

faq.q: If I sell something for ten dollars, and it cost me three dollars, what is my profit?
faq.a: Your profit is seven dollars because you take the ten dollars you earned and subtract the three dollars you spent.
asks: What is the profit if I sell five items?
Can I make a profit if I spend a lot?
What if my costs are more than my sales?

facts: Revenue is the total amount of money earned from sales.
Costs are the expenses incurred to produce goods or services.
A good business idea often solves a specific problem.

quiz.say: If you sell 10 cakes for a total of 100 dollars, and your ingredients cost 30 dollars, what is your profit?
quiz.why: You take the total money you earned, which is one hundred dollars, and subtract the money you spent on ingredients, which is thirty dollars. This leaves you with seventy dollars.

wrong.0: This only calculates the total cost and ignores the money you brought in.
wrong.2: Adding the costs to the revenue is incorrect because costs are money you already spent.
wrong.3: Only looking at the number of cakes sold ignores the money you actually earned.

quiz.say: A baker spends five dollars on flour and sugar to make loaves of bread. If he sells the loaves for twenty dollars total, what is his profit?
quiz.why: The total money earned is twenty dollars, and the total money spent was five dollars. Subtracting five from twenty gives you fifteen dollars profit.

wrong.0: Adding the costs and revenue together gives a number that is too high.
wrong.1: This only tells you how much the ingredients cost, not how much you earned.
wrong.2: Subtracting the cost from the revenue, but forgetting to account for all the sales.

quiz.say: If a student sells handmade bookmarks for five dollars each, and the materials cost one dollar per bookmark, what is the profit per bookmark?
quiz.show: Profit per item = Sale Price - Cost
quiz.why: To find the profit for one bookmark, you subtract the cost of materials, one dollar, from the selling price, five dollars. This leaves four dollars profit.

wrong.1: Adding the selling price and the cost together gives a number that is too high.
wrong.2: This only shows the selling price and ignores the money spent on materials.
wrong.3: This only shows the cost of the materials and ignores the money you earned.
